Recent indicators show solid growth and a strong labor market, but inflation has stalled above target. Holding the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50 percent and signaling no cuts until “greater confidence” aligns with inflation-forecast targeting and addresses discretionary inflation bias; the slower balance-sheet runoff (reducing Treasury redemptions from $60B to $25B) modestly eases term-structure pressures without changing the overall restrictive stance.

FSR overlay: The Financial Stability Report highlights elevated vulnerabilities that temper the otherwise growth-positive read—valuation pressures, credit quality strains, structural vulnerabilities in money market funds, elevated interest rate volatility, and Treasury market intermediation risks tied to hedge fund futures/basis trades. It also flags ongoing concerns around commercial real estate (notably office vacancy), concentrated triple-B corporate debt, and broader macro-financial risks (public debt, geopolitical tensions, and China-related downside risks). These factors argue for a more cautious net tone despite the slight dovish nuance from slower QT.

Bottom line: Growth-positive but inflation- and stability-cautious; QT slowdown is a minor easing, yet overall restrictive policy and FSR-identified vulnerabilities dampen risk sentiment.
